full_judgment:
2. Case of the petitioners, in short, is as follows: The lands of CS Plot Nos. 677, 680 and 681 originally belonged to Wazir Bibi and by inheritance; transfer and abandonment of the tenancy Shamsun Nahar Begum, Syed Mohammad Abdul Motaleb and Abdul Hamid became owners and possessors of the same. Thereafter Abdul Hamid orally gifted his share to his cousins, petitioner Nos. 1-3. Similarly Syed Mohammad Abdul Motaleb orally gifted his share to the petitioner Nos. 4 and 5. Shamsun Nahar Begum died leaving petitioner Nos. 1-3 as her son and daughters and only legal heirs to inherit her share. On 10.4.1950 an area of 32.50 acre of land was requisitioned in LA Case No. 29 of 1949-50 including 0'10 acre of CS plot No. 680, 0'13 are of CS plot No. 681 being parts of these plots and entire 0'28 acre of CS plot No. 677 of Mouja Dhanmondi owned and possessed by the petitioners for Diplomatic Colony. Thereafter on 24.1.51 some area of requisitioned land including the said land of the petitioners  were de-requisitioned but possession of the same was not delivered to the petitioners or their predecessors-in-interest. There- after by Gazette Notification dated 4.10.1951 said requisitioned land was acquired under section 5(7) of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948. By order dated 5.5.1952 payment of compensation in respect of CS Plot Nos. 677 and 680 was stopped. By Gazette Notification dated 11.11.1954 original Gazette Notification dated 4.10.1951 was amended deleting "for Diplomatic Colony." Thereafter 20 acres of the said acquired land was made over to the Bangladesh Scientific and Industrial Research Council in 1955 and remaining 12.50 acre of land remaining unutilized must be deemed to have been de-requisitioned. The land of the petitioners is still lying vacant though covered by the boundary walls of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research. In spite of petitions filed by the petitioners and their predecessors-in-interest possession of the disputed land was not made over to them. Thereafter on the application of the petitioners by letter dated 21.12. 1982 Senior Member, Martial Law Vigilance Team recommended to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) Dhaka to take steps to rectify the irregularities in including 12.50 acres in the Gazette Notification for acquisition by another Gazette Notification as the same was de-requisitioned in 1951. Thereafter by Memo dated 6.3.1983 Section Officer of the Ministry of Law and Land Reforms asked the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) to submit a report with a map and in reply thereto by Memo dated 10.5.1983 Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) forwarded a map to the said Section Officer showing the area of acquired and de-requisitioned land including petitioner's said land. But the Government did not take any steps to restore vacant possession of the disputed land to the petitioners in spite of receipt of the said report and map. Thereafter on the application of the petitioners Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms called for a report from the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) Dhaka who by Memo dated 29.11.1984 stated that 12.50 acre of land out of 32.50 acre of land was withdrawn from acquisition but possession of the said de-requisitioned land was not restored to the owners thereof and disputed land of the petitioners are lying vacant within the boundary walls of Bangladesh Council for Scientific and Industrial Research. But instead of restoring possession of the disputed land to the petitioners Government again by Memo dated 6.11.1986 asked for another report in consultation with the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and with their opinion in the matter. Thereafter by Memo dated 20.10.1986 Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) Dhaka informed the Government that an area of 6.27 acre of land in addition to 20 acre of allotted land lies within the boundary walls constructed by the Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research. But the respondents having failed to restore possession of the disputed land which was de-requisitioned the petitioners served notice dated 14.3.1987 demanding justice in the matter to put the petitioners in possession of the disputed land. The respondents are legally bound to restore possession of the disputed land to the petitioners. 

 4. The petitioners filed two affidavits-in-reply to the said affidavits-in-opposition stating that they are the owners of the disputed land and title of their predecessor was recorded in CS Khatians in respect of Plot No. 681 and declared in respect of Plot Nos. 677 and 680 in Title Suit No. 32 of 1950 and LA Collector also admitted their predecessor's claim to compensation by correcting the awards. 

 10. It is an admitted fact that an area of 32.50 acre of land including the disputed land was requisitioned by the respondent No. 2 Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 10.4.1950 in LA Case No. 29 of 1949-50 under the provisions of section 3 of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act and subsequently acquired under the provisions of section 5 of the said Act by notification dated 24.9.1951 published in the Gazette dated 4.10.1951 for the Diplomatic Colony at Dhanmondi but by notification dated 13.10.1954 published in the Gazette dated 11.11.1954 the said purpose of acquisition was deleted. It is also admitted that an area of 20 acres of land out of the acquired 32.50 acres was allotted and leased out to the respondent No. 4, BCSIR for construction of its laboratories in 1955. It is not denied by the petitioners that in 1957 Government allotted another area of 7'60 acres of land including the disputed land to the respondent No. 4 and delivered possession of the same to the respondent No. 4. Admittedly, the disputed land is within the boundary walls of the respondent No. 4. Petitioners contended that the disputed land is lying vacant but the respondent Nos. 1 and 4 on the other hand contended that the disputed land is covered by constructions within the boundary walls of the respondent No. 4. 

 12. It appears from the certified copy of the CS Khatians annexed to the affidavit-in-reply that land of CS Plot No. 681 belonged to Uzir Bibi, Nejamat Ali and others. It also appears from the certified copies of the judgment and decree passed on 26.12.52 in Title Suit No. 32 of 1950 of the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka annexed to the affidavit- in-reply that title of Shamsun Nahar and others in the compensation awarded in respect of lands of CS Plot Nos. 677 and 680 was declared. It also appears from the order dated 5.2.52 in LA Case No 29 of 1949-50 annexed to the affidavit-in-reply that award for compensation in respect of CS Plot Nos. 677 and 680 was corrected in favour of the said Shamsun Nahar, Abdul Mutalab, Abdul Aziz and Abdul Hamid, predecessors of the petitioners in pursuance of the aforesaid judgment and decree. But there is no assertion by the petitioners that after correction of the award no payment was made to those awardees Shamsun Nahar and others. There is nothing on record to show that the petitioners were admitted as owners of the disputed land by the respondents who dispute their claim of title and possession therein. We cannot examine and decide the title of the petitioners in the disputed land in writ jurisdiction. Moreover, it is the function of the Deputy Commissioner to decide the claim of compensation under section 7A of the said Act or the Civil Court. Similarly it is the function of the Deputy Commissioner under section 8 of the said Act to decide the claim of any persons for restoration of the land. Only when the Deputy Commissioner exercised the jurisdiction without lawful authority this Court can exercise the same.
